title: Matthews et al. (2016) global plate boundary evolution since the late Paleozoic
citation: Matthews, K. J., Maloney, K. T., Zahirovic, S., Williams, S. E., Seton, M., and Müller, R. D., 2016. Global plate boundary evolution and kinematics since the late Paleozoic. Global and Planetary Change, 146, 226-250.

relationship: A separate lineage from the Merdith line: published in 2016, built around plate boundary evolution rather than a billion-year synthesis, and carried in shapefiles rather than GPML. It reaches 410 Ma, so it says nothing before that.
limitations: Covers the late Palaeozoic onward only. Its geometry is continental polygons rather than the coastline-and-continent pair the other models ship, so the outlines are coarser.
